article.articleSummary: Cholera outbreak risk persists in Ethiopia amid protracted conflict, climate shocks, displacement, and weak WASH services. article.articleSummary: Chikungunya outbreak in Gandara, Samar, Philippines, with 84 confirmed cases in the villages of Ngoso and Catorse de Agosto. Seek medical attention promptly; avoid NSAIDs like ibuprofen or aspirin without a clinician's guidance, as these can complicate dengue diagnosis.

article.articleHeadline: Sewage pollution, disease caused Panzath spring fish deaths: SKUAST-K
article.articleSummary: As of 10 July 2026, severe sewage contamination degrades water quality at Panzath springs (Panzath Nag) in Qazigund, Anantnag, triggering ecological stress, oxygen depletion, and disease in the indigenous Schizothorax and mass fish mortality. This is Kashmir’s sixth mass fish mortality in six months, with prior events at Nagbal, Andernag (Anantnag), Chamgund (Kulgam), Zainapora (Shopian), Beehama (Ganderbal), and Martand (Mattan).

article.articleHeadline: Monsoon is here and so is the Season of RSV Pneumonia and Chest infections
article.articleSummary: RSV is the leading cause of pneumonia in infants, contributing up to 40% of pneumonia hospitalizations in babies under 1 year. During India's monsoon season, RSV may begin as a cold but can progress to bronchiolitis or pneumonia with fast breathing, chest indrawing, wheeze, poor feeding, lethargy, or requiring hospitalization or ICU care. In infants, RSV infection can have long-term implications such as wheezing or asthma. Prevention centers on hand hygiene, avoiding close contact with sick people, limiting crowded indoor exposure, cleaning surfaces, good ventilation, continued breastfeeding, and up-to-date immunizations; clinicians also discuss RSV preventive options. Global use of long-acting antibody protection against RSV is implemented in about 25 countries (US, Middle East, Europe) and is now available in India. Most babies recover with prompt assessment and, if needed, oxygen, hydration, and monitoring; urgent care is needed for rapid breathing, chest indrawing, poor feeding, dehydration, bluish lips, or lethargy.

article.articleHeadline: Public Health reassures about the cyclosporiasis outbreak originating from Michigan.
article.articleSummary: Public Health Agency of Canada reassures that the Cyclospora outbreak linked to Michigan has not spread to Canada as of 10 July 2026. Michigan reported infections rising from about 170 to 1,251 by July, a rise from roughly 50 cases annually. The outbreak source remains unknown. Cyclospora causes watery diarrhea for six to seven weeks, with bloating, gas, nausea, fatigue, abdominal cramps, appetite and weight loss, and mild fever. Transmission occurs when contaminated water used in irrigation or processing contaminates produce. Canada reports no Cyclospora in drinking water; foods are not typically affected domestically, though imports from Peru, Cuba, India, Nepal, Mexico, Guatemala, the Dominican Republic, and parts of Southeast Asia can carry it. Foods linked include raspberries, blackberries, basil, cilantro, mesclun, and salads. Diagnosis via stool sample; treatment with prescription medication; symptoms lessen in 2–3 days, but recovery may take weeks; prevention: cook imported produce or choose Canada-grown produce.

article.articleHeadline: Dengue fever can still be contracted in apartment buildings because of these seven factors.
article.articleSummary: Seven hidden water sources in apartment buildings enable Aedes aegypti mosquitoes to breed and sustain dengue transmission: air-conditioner drip trays, flower vases, plant-water saucers, balconies, drainage trenches, mop buckets, and fridge condensation trays. After rain, tiny, seemingly clean water accumulations in these spots can harbor larvae, enabling local transmission, as Aedes aegypti bites primarily during the day and can bite multiple people in the same area. A high-rise setting requires awareness since mosquitoes can travel via hallways, elevators, or shared spaces. A simple, weekly 10-minute check can reduce risk: one-minute balcony cleanup; two minutes plant pot and vase cleaning; two minutes bathroom/kitchen; two minutes air-conditioner/fridge drainage; final minute ensure all containers are covered and trash removed. Spraying insecticides only kills adults; larvae remain if water is present, so community-wide larval control is essential. Not every fever is dengue, but vigilance is advised during the rainy season.

article.articleHeadline: Comprehensive actions protect families in Santa Rosa from dengue
article.articleSummary: Dengue in Santa Rosa is being addressed through comprehensive vector-control actions under the Integrated and Inclusive Care Model based on Health Care Networks. Health brigades are visiting communities to eliminate Aedes aegypti breeding sites, conducting entomological surveys, applying treatments to suppress larval habitats, and performing fogging in various communities. The program also strengthens mosquito surveillance and control. Health teams advise families to keep yards and homes free of water-holding containers and to remove items that collect standing water. By bringing prevention directly to communities and promoting active public participation, these measures aim to interrupt the dengue transmission chain and protect collective health.

article.articleHeadline: New dengue virus case identified on Oʻahu: DOH
article.articleSummary: On July 10, 2026, Hawaiʻi Department of Health confirmed a new travel-associated dengue case on Oʻahu, bringing Hawaii’s 2026 total to six. The infection occurred during travel in a region where dengue is common; Hawaii is not endemic, and current cases are travelers, with low risk of local transmission. Dengue spreads from an infected person to a mosquito and then to others. Symptoms include fever, nausea, vomiting, rash, and body aches, typically lasting 2–7 days, with most people recovering within a week. Regions with year-round dengue risk include Central and South America (Brazil, Mexico), Asia (Philippines), Africa, the Middle East, the Pacific (American Samoa, FSM, Marshall Islands, Palau), and the Caribbean (Puerto Rico). As of July 2026, higher-than-usual activity is reported in Samoa, Vietnam, Colombia, Cambodia, Maldives, Mali, New Caledonia, Timor-Leste, Bolivia, and Guyana. CDC recommends EPA-registered repellents, long sleeves/pants, and sleeping in screened or air-conditioned rooms; suspected cases can call 808-586-4586.

article.articleHeadline: Foundation raises concern about new HIV infection spread in Sunyani Municipality
article.articleSummary: In Sunyani Municipality, Ghana, new HIV infections are rising, with no exact counts released. MIHOSO International Foundation, in partnership with GHANET, is implementing an HIV Self-Testing (HIVST) project distributing oral-quick and blood-based self-test kits to vulnerable groups and the wider community. Self-testing yields private results in 20–40 minutes. Monitoring and Evaluation Officer Arnold Sopaal urged sexually active individuals, especially youth, to know their HIV status and adopt safer sex practices, including condom use; he cautioned against premarital sex and multiple partners. He noted ongoing stigma and discrimination hindering prevention, stating HIV is now like any ordinary disease and calling for reduced stigma to curb spread. The program aims to help bring the spread under control by enabling discreet testing and private results.

article.articleHeadline: Flood-hit food could trigger cholera, typhoid outbreaks - Environmental Health Director warns - Adomonline.com
article.articleSummary: Floodwaters in Anloga, Volta Region, submerged refuse dumps and toilet facilities, increasing contamination risk and potential outbreaks of cholera, typhoid and other waterborne diseases. Volta Regional Environmental Health Director Stella Kumedzro warned residents, food vendors, and market women not to consume or sell food that came into contact with floodwaters. The warning accompanies a nationwide two-day clean-up aimed at restoring sanitation and reducing disease risk following recent floods. Officials and volunteers cleared choked drains, removed refuse, and rehabilitated public spaces to curb transmission. Kumedzro urged sustained hygiene practices, proper waste disposal, and reporting of suspected food contamination to health authorities, stressing that environmental sanitation must be ongoing, not a one-off event. The message underscores ongoing flood-related health risks in Anloga and surrounding areas.

article.articleHeadline: Multi-Country Bundibugyo Ebola Virus Disease Outbreak Situation Report No. 8 (29 June - 5 July 2026)
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease (BVD) outbreak affecting the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda: as of 4 July, DRC has confirmed over 1,500 BVD cases, while Uganda reports 20 cases as of 5 July with no new Ugandan cases during the reporting period. Cross-border movements and population displacement are driving transmission, prompting urgent, rapid responses to protect mobile populations. The International Organization for Migration (IOM) is expanding surge operations, prioritizing cross-border communities, border points of entry (PoEs) and points of control (PoCs) to guide broader public health actions. The response aligns with IASC scale-up activation for infectious disease events. Priority 1a countries are DRC and Uganda; Priority 1b countries are Burundi, Rwanda, and South Sudan (elevated cross-border transmission risk). Preparedness activities are under way in Priority 2 countries—Angola, Central African Republic, Ethiopia, Kenya, Republic of the Congo, United Republic of Tanzania, and Zambia—co-leading PoE efforts continent-wide.
